# 01. Database Overview — FACET CRM

## Provider
Supabase (PostgreSQL), Bahrain region (me-south-1)  
URL: `https://qndpfbmniqxkegzmzcmh.supabase.co`

---

## Extensions

| Extension | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `uuid-ossp` | UUID generation (`uuid_generate_v4()`) |
| `pg_trgm` | Trigram fuzzy text matching for duplicate detection |

---

## Schema Conventions

### Auto-Generated Codes
Every primary entity has a human-readable code generated by trigger on INSERT:
- Companies → `CUST-00001`, `CUST-00002`, ...
- Projects → `PROJ-00001`, ...
- Activities → `ACT-00001`, ...
- Quotations → `QUO-00001`, ...
- Contacts → `CON-00001`, ...

Sequences: `customer_code_seq`, `project_code_seq`, `activity_code_seq`, `quotation_code_seq`, `contact_code_seq`

### Timestamps
- `created_at` — always set by DEFAULT now(), never updated
- `updated_at` — updated by `set_updated_at()` trigger on every UPDATE where it exists
- `timestamptz` — all timestamps store timezone info (UTC internally, converted to Asia/Riyadh in application logic)

### Primary Keys
All tables use `uuid` primary keys generated by `uuid_generate_v4()`.

### Soft Deletes
The system does NOT use soft deletes. Records are hard-deleted when removed. Company deletion cascades to contacts and related company_reps entries.

| `project_reps` | Rep-to-project assignments | Same order as projects |

| `quotation_services` | Services per quotation | 0–4 per quotation |

| `company_holidays` | Team-wide excused days | < 20 per year |
| `rep_absences` | Individual excused periods | < 50 per year |
| `project_history` | Stage/SQM change audit log | Grows continuously |

## Critical Design Decisions

### Junction Tables Over Text Columns
The `shared_with` text column (old approach) is completely removed. All rep-to-entity access is via:
- `company_reps` — links reps to companies
- `project_reps` — links reps to projects

**Never add a `shared_with` text column to any table. Never write code that queries `shared_with`.**

### SECURITY DEFINER RPCs for Atomic Inserts
Because RLS prevents a rep from inserting into `company_reps` and `project_reps` directly during the same transaction as creating the parent record, all atomic creation operations use PostgreSQL functions with `SECURITY DEFINER`. These functions run as the postgres user (bypassing RLS safely server-side).

### Legacy Cache Columns
Three columns exist as performance caches from the old architecture. They are redundant but kept intentionally:
- `projects.company_name` — cache of the company name at project creation time
- `projects.assigned_rep_id` — cache of the primary rep UUID
- `activities.rep_name` — cache of the rep name at activity submission time

Do not rely on these for access control. Use the junction tables. These will be dropped in a future cleanup phase.

## Source of Truth Statement

**`schema.sql` in the GitHub repository is NOT the authoritative source of truth for the production schema.** It is a documentation artifact that may lag behind production changes made via the Supabase SQL Editor.

The authoritative source of truth is the live Supabase database. When in doubt about a column, constraint, or policy, query the Supabase dashboard directly.

To check production constraints:
```sql
SELECT constraint_name, constraint_definition
FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc
JOIN information_schema.check_constraints cc USING (constraint_name)
WHERE tc.table_name = 'your_table';
```
